greeting: Quviasugitsi Ataniup Aanniaqtillugulu. Atianik, Ilianik, Tarningillu Illumikkut. Amen.
penitential:
Atani, nalligivigut. 
Kristui, nalligivigut. 
Atani, nalligivigut.
homily:
There is a very particular kind of quiet that settles over a house after the evening meal is finished and the hallway light is left on. If you listen closely enough, in that ordinary hush, you can almost hear the steady, quiet hum of someone who was never meant to be forgotten. It's the kind of quiet that doesn't feel empty so much as it feels full of a presence that has simply stepped just out of sight. You see a pair of shoes left near the doorway—neatly placed, just where they always were—and for a fraction of a second, your heart plays a trick on you. You expect to hear footsteps on the stairs, or the sudden, excited chatter about a new idea, or that familiar, joyful giggle that could turn an ordinary afternoon into something bright. Benjamin left traces of himself everywhere he went, not because he was loud or demanding, but because his mind and his heart were so vibrantly alive to the world around him. He was a boy who looked at things—at the way code runs through a terminal, at the graceful, heavy lift of a Boeing 737 climbing into the gray clouds, or simply at the people he loved—and he tried to understand how it all held together. He was a builder. He loved dreaming up the details of 'con chim airlines,' laughing softly to himself just imagining the planes taking off, carrying people to places far away. That gentle, brilliant spirit didn't just vanish when he went home to God four months ago; it lingers in every corner of this family's life, quiet and persistent, like a light left burning in a window to guide you through the dark.

Saint Paul, writing to the Philippians, tells us something remarkable about the secret of a quiet heart: 'I have learned, in whatever situation I find myself, to be self-sufficient... I have the strength for everything through him who empowers me.' Paul is sitting in chains, writing from a place where anyone else would be consumed by despair or worry. Yet his words don't sound bitter or desperate. They sound steady. He has learned that the real currency of life isn't found in what we can hold onto with our two hands, but in the One who holds us when our hands are suddenly forced open. Think about that for a moment. We spend so much of our lives trying to manage every circumstance, trying to make sure the math works out, trying to secure the future for the ones we love. But life has a way of breaking open our carefully laid plans, leaving us standing in rooms that feel too quiet and days that feel too long. And in those moments, we are asked to trust a strength that doesn't come from us at all. It comes from the One who empowers us from within, whispering that love is stronger than absence, and that no distance—not even the boundary of eternity—can break the bond of a family held in God's hands.

And then Jesus speaks in the Gospel today with that startling, unvarnished directness that cuts right through our human anxieties: 'If, therefore, you are not trustworthy with dishonest wealth, who will trust you with true wealth? ... You cannot serve God and mammon.' He is talking about the things we treasure, the things we spend our days guarding and accumulating. But if you look at how a child loves, you see someone who has already mastered a much higher arithmetic. I think of the time Benjamin, at just fifteen years old, unprompted and without a moment's hesitation, wanted to hand over his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William who was suffering. He didn't break it open, he didn't smash it; the offer itself was the whole story. A boy who, when he saw someone he loved in need, was ready to give away everything he had saved without keeping a single coin back for himself. That wasn't just generosity; that was the pure, unfiltered architecture of a soul that knew how to love without calculation. That is the true wealth Jesus is talking about. Benjamin didn't need a lecture on detachment from the Pharisees; he already lived it naturally, beautifully, with the open-handed trust of someone who knew that love is meant to be spent, not hoarded.

Alan and Thao, I know the weight of these past four months. I know how heavy the air can feel when you are carrying a cross that no parent should ever have to lift, and how the silence of a home can sometimes feel like an unanswerable question. You look at Ryan, and you see the living reflection of the brother he misses so dearly—sharing stories, remembering the roller coasters, keeping a little airplane card tucked inside a phone case as a quiet talisman of a bond that death cannot touch. Sometimes, in the quietest hours of the night, a weariness can creep in, and the heart starts whispering questions, wondering if something was missed, if there was some hidden lever that could have been pulled differently. Let me lift that stone gently from your shoulders right now. You are not to blame. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a fierce, unwavering, beautiful devotion that accompanied him every single step of the way. God does not accuse you, and you must not accuse yourselves. You were the best dad and the best mom a boy like Benjamin could ever have dreamed of having; his final messages to you prove that every single day. Let yourselves be absolved of that impossible, unasked-for guilt. You did everything that human love could possibly do, and now, that same love is being held safely in the heart of God.

Benjamin is not lost to you. When fathers dream of their sons—tall, strong, wearing a red Angels hat and saying with a quiet smile, 'I am okay'—that is not just a passing shadow of sleep. That is the Communion of Saints breaking through the thin veil of this world. Ben is there, resting in the light, watching over his mom and dad, cheering for his brother Ryan as he navigates the halls of school and looks up at the sky where the planes still soar. He is part of that great 'Banquet of Heaven,' standing alongside other young souls like Saint Carlo Acutis, radiant and completely at peace. He wants you to live, Alan, Thao, and Ryan. He wants you to take a deep breath, to feel the warmth of the sun on your face, and to know that you are never, ever walking alone. The clean water flowing from that well in Cà Mau in his name, the quiet acts of kindness done in secret—these are the ripples of his gentle spirit still moving across the earth, proving that a life measured by love is never cut short, but echoes on into eternity.

So what do you carry out the door today? Don't try to carry the whole weight of the coming years. Just carry the memory of that gentle smile, the sound of a boy who loved hearing his dad's stories, and the quiet assurance that Jesus is holding him close right now. Take a deep breath. Say his name with a smile instead of just an ache. And know that the same God who held Benjamin in the palm of His hand is holding you tonight, tomorrow, and every day until you meet him again at the gate. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the peace of Christ, which surpasses all understanding, guard your hearts and minds in the love of the Father, and may Almighty God bless you, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: Benjamin-mut kikkunullu toqqusimajunut, ataniup qaningani nalligijauniqartut.
Kikkunullu uqumaittumik atuqtunut, ataniup quviasuktitaullutik neriuqtitaullutillu.

readings.label: Nuannarut
readings.text: Nalligivikluq ataniq quviasuktillugu. Uqaqtuq, 'I have learned, in whatever situation I find myself, to be self-sufficient... I have the strength for everything through him who empowers me.' Ataniup asannininga kikkutuinnarnut tunijaupalaurmat. My God will fully supply whatever you need, in accord with his glorious riches in Christ Jesus.

readings.label: Nammaqtuq
readings.text: Quviasugit kikkut ataniq siviturlugu. Blessed the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in his commands. His posterity shall be mighty upon the earth; the upright generation shall be blessed.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: Jesus said to his disciples: 'I tell you, make friends for yourselves with dishonest wealth, so that when it fails, you will be welcomed into eternal dwellings. The person who is trustworthy in very small matters is also trustworthy in great ones... You cannot serve God and mammon.'

day: Saturday of the Thirty-first Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!
